extracted.intended_audience: marketers, content creators, and non-designers creating infographics
extracted.subtask_description: Practical best-practices for creating clear, engaging, shareable infographics — from planning and layout to charts, color, typography, and iteration. Aimed at people using templates or DIY tools to produce infographic visuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan your infographic design
rubrics_metrics.description: Define your goal, audience and key message before starting visuals; find the infographic's story and design to support that story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start by thinking of the story you want your data to tell (angle determines what information to include). Keep the infographic focused and purposeful—start with a clear message and organize content in a logical flow (beginning, middle, end). Use visuals to guide the reader’s eye and simplify complex ideas. Create an infographic outline (headers, data, design details) as a brain-dump and then refine. Examples: use numbered boxes and arrows for process flow; plan for limited space and prioritize content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow data visualization best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Design charts and data presentation so data is easy to understand, accurate, and engaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the best chart type for the data and the story: column/ bar graphs for comparisons, line charts for trends over time, pie charts for parts-of-a-whole, scatter plots for correlations/outliers. Keep charts simple enough to be grasped in ten seconds or less. Always cite your infographic data sources. Be willing to use unconventional charts if they convey the data effectively (e.g., scatter for outliers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage visual color and contrast
rubrics_metrics.description: Use color contrast to create impact and organize information by making elements prominent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pair complementary colors to make headlines pop (example: dark blue with bright orange). Use contrast between background and bold-colored shapes to attract attention. Use tinted images or backgrounds contrasted with chart overlays to add context. Consider color for sectioning and hierarchy. Be mindful of accessibility/readability when choosing contrasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrast using typography sizes (hierarchy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish clear typographic hierarchy so readers immediately understand the subject and flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Header should be the largest text, followed by subheader and body copy; header must communicate subject instantly. Use typography to emphasize title and hierarchy; bold, large headlines and specific subheaders help readers know what information to expect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write a compelling title
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a catchy, descriptive title that communicates the most important information immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the three Cs: be clear, crisp and concise. Headlines with numbers tend to grab attention and encourage social shares. Use typography to emphasize the title (big, bold headline with a specific subheader). Ensure the title tells viewers what they will get from the infographic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a grid design
rubrics_metrics.description: Design on grids or wireframes to organize elements, maintain alignment, and create consistent spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grids help align items (especially in tall infographics) and create consistent margins. Keep enough space between elements and the canvas edge to avoid visual tension. Rule of thumb: keep objects and elements at least 20px (one grid square) away from the edge. Use consistent margins across the design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the right infographic layout
rubrics_metrics.description: Pick a layout that suits your content and data (one-column, two-column comparison, staggered, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose one-column for a clean, minimal look; split into two columns for comparisons; use staggered two-column for a creative layout. Select templates/layouts that guide the reader’s eye according to your story. Follow step-by-step template-selection guidance if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate different design elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Mix images, charts, icons, and typography to set tone and convey meaning; keep text supporting visuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typography sets tone — choose fonts appropriate to context (e.g., Helvetica/Arial/Times for professional settings; elegant fonts for formal events). Limit text; rely on icons, dates, headers, and visuals. Avoid decorative/script typefaces that harm legibility. Limit use of fonts to a maximum of three types (a tasteful pair of brand fonts often works best). Consider using one font for numbers/statistics and another for body text to create hierarchy. Ensure legibility at the sizes used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use photographs carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Use photography to add context while maintaining cohesion, style, and readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stock photos (Pixabay, Unsplash, Pikwizard) are acceptable but can look generic—choose photos with cohesive style, similar lighting, backdrops, and symmetry. Use consistent photographic style (e.g., solid color on white background or black-and-white for a newspaper feel). Avoid photos that take up too much space—crop or frame them into rectangles so they support rather than dominate the design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain visual balance (symmetrical or asymmetrical) so the composition feels cohesive and pleasing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribute visual weight across the infographic—if heavy visuals appear at the top, balance them with heavier elements lower down. Symmetrical balance suits comparisons; asymmetrical balance can make layouts more dynamic. For timelines, alternate text boxes between sides for asymmetry. Choose the type of balance based on your content and desired tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use color effectively (scheme and tone)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide on a color scheme in advance and use color to set tone, brand alignment, and sectioning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design with two or three main colors and additional accent colors. Choose tone according to purpose (neutral blues/greens for business; brand colors when appropriate; brighter hues for fun designs). Avoid large amounts of dark or neon colors that strain the eyes. Use blocks of color to create sections and guide scrolling. Consider brand consistency when sharing widely. Tools: color palette generators and curated palette lists (pastel, fall, blue palettes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep style elements uniform across the infographic to avoid clutter and improve readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent icon style (filled vs line art), image style, font choices, and a consistent color palette throughout. Brand consistency helps recognition when sharing publicly. Inconsistent styles look unprofessional and distract from the message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage negative space
rubrics_metrics.description: Use blank space (margins, spacing between elements and lines) to give readers breathing room and improve comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid clutter—negative space improves comprehension (design experts claim increased spacing can improve comprehension by up to 20%). Ensure adequate space between paragraphs and margins. Practical tip: if using 16pt font, set line height no less than 1.2. Use spacing to make information easier to process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice and iterate (revise before publishing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expect multiple revisions; iterate designs and solicit feedback to improve quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design a few versions and learn from duds. Use ready-made templates, examples, or AI generators to shorten the learning curve. Ask someone else to review designs to catch issues you missed. Regenerate and edit as needed until the design and message are clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid information overload
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not cram too much data or too many ideas into an infographic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Too much data overwhelms readers. Focus on key points and simplify complex information—prioritize what the audience must remember rather than everything you know about a topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid poor color contrast
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure sufficient contrast between text and background and between adjacent elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low contrast reduces readability—use contrasting colors for text and background to ensure legibility and accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inconsistent design elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not mix incompatible fonts, icon styles, or image treatments within a single infographic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mixing different fonts and styles looks unprofessional and clutters the design. Keep icons, fonts, and image styles consistent to maintain cohesion and readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid lack of visual hierarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize information so readers know where to look first and which elements are most important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use size, positioning, typography, color, and spacing to guide attention and establish a clear reading order. Without hierarchy, the reader may be unsure how to process information.
